# RH-16520 [VNCNMS][VCTC] RTE Error generated by TimeOut function when E2E SignalGroup is used across cores

> [!jira] Waiting for Customer · Medium · [[ZHANG_Junsheng_(ETAS-ECMXSF-CN)|Junsheng ZHANG]] · 更新于 2026-09-09T16:00:10.000+0200
> [在 Jira 中打开](https://rtahotline.etas.com/jira/browse/RH-16520)

> 标签：#jira/comp/rta-rte #jira/label/vncnms

## 描述

Hi hotline,

My customer used E2E SignalGroup in the project and communicated across cores. In this case, there will be undefined variables generated in the TimeOut function generated by RTE;

For example, in the following figure, 'Rte_Rx_000762' is not defined;

![[RH-16520-image001.png]]

This Signalgroup is received by Core0 and Core4 respectively, but the RTE code will have the above problem;

![[RH-16520-image002.png]]

![[RH-16520-image003.png]]

![[RH-16520-image004.png]]

As shown in the image below, black represents SignalGroup that does not cross cores, red represents SignalGroup that only crosses cores, green represents multi-core applications, and SinalGroup exists across both cores;

Only black, which means it cannot cross cores, can generate the correct RTE code; We believe this is a bug related to E2E and SignalGroup in RTE. Please help provide a quick solution; This has affected the client's compilation and development work;

![[RH-16520-image-2026-06-30-10-53-26-510.png]]

> [!note]+ 2026-08-25 18:28 · [[Vamsi_Kiran_Koduri|Vamsi Kiran Koduri]]
> Hello  [[Ho_Anh_Dang_(MSETA-Hub-CN)|Dang Ho Anh]] ,
>
> We analyzed reported observations in generated code and confirm there are no major findings apart from "composite.status getting updated two times in Rte_COMCbk function" which can be minor fix and not blocking.
>
> **why reported observations are incorrect:**
>
> The alive timeout is not configured on the Rport of SWC which is mapped to same partition --> so it is expected to not generate anything relevant to timeout for this which then rules out Test case2/3 findings.
>
> Having postfix at the end of Ioc Channel function names are okay if the same names are generated by RTAOS which is the case here. OsNeeds generated by RTE has receiver ID's for these IOC channels which will inform RTAOS to generate consistent names --> So this is not an issue.
>
> FYI [[Matthew_Greenfield|Matthew Greenfield]] ,[[Jack_Whitham|Jack Whitham]]

> [!note]+ 2026-07-01 12:15 · [[Ho_Anh_Dang_(MSETA-Hub-CN)|Dang Ho Anh]]
> Dear [Koduri Vamsi Kiran (ETAS-ECM/XPC-Abt1)](https://confluence.etas-dev.com/display/~kod4abt)
>
> Please find my analysis for the ticket below:
>  * Setup: The test project contains a signal group ({_}SG_ISigGrp_C1_CDA_IBRS_ADASToqCtrl_Group_C1_CDA_IBRS_ADASToqCtrl_Can_Network_3_Channel_CAN_Rx{_}) which is processed by Com module on core 0; this signal group will be received by E2E_SWC (core 0) and Muti_SWC (core 4).
>  * {*}Case 1{*}: Rte option -{-}strict-unconnected-rport-check=off -nts --os-define-osenv=RTAOS40 --exclusive-area-optimization=disable --os-output-param=changed --notimestamps --use-partition-sections=on -err=xml --deviate-bsw-any-partition=1 --deviate-split-swci-support=on --deviate-prefer-no-empty-executions=on --force-basic-tasks{-}  -error-report=xml --text-value-spec-policy=symbolic-pdav-always --client-server-global-optimization=1
>  ** In Rte_COMCbkTOut_* function, **the variable Rte_Rx_000875 is not defined in Rte.**
>  ** ![[RH-16520-image-2026-07-01-16-30-16-018.png]]
>  ** In the Rte_Read_E2E_SWC_* function, it called _IocRead_Rte_Rx_000875_0(&composite)_ to get the status of the signal group. -> **This seems wrong because E2E_SWC and Com are both running on core 0.**
>  ** In the Rte_Read_Muti_SWC_* function, it called _IocRead_Rte_Rx_000875_1(&composite)_ to get the status of the signal group.
>  ** In Rte_ComCbk_* of this signal group, it calls IocWrite_Rte_Rx_000875(&composite) to update the status.
>  * {*}Case 2{*}: Rte option case 1 + (--no-optimized-ioc-channels)
>  ** In Rte_COMCbkTOut_* function, both variables Rte_Rx_000921 and Rte_Rx_000922_status are defined by Rte.
>  ** In the Rte_Read_E2E_SWC_* function, it called _Rte_memcpy(&composite, &Rte_Rx_000921, sizeof(Rte_Rx_000921_Composite_Type))_ to get the status of the signal group. -> I think it's okay because E2E_SWC and Com (core 0) are running on the same core.
>  ** In the Rte_Read_Muti_SWC_* function, it called _IocRead_Rte_Rx_000922(&composite)_ to get the status of the signal group.
>  ** In Rte_ComCbk_* of this signal group, it calls the below to function to update the status
>  *** Rte_memcpy(&Rte_Rx_000921, &composite, sizeof(Rte_Rx_000921_Composite_Type));
>  *** IocWrite_Rte_Rx_000922(&composite);
>  ** {*}With this setup, I think the issue is that the status is updated in Rte_Rx_000922_status in Rte_COMCbkTOut_{*}, but this variable is not used by Rte_Read_Muti_SWC_* function to retrieve the status.*
>  * **Case 3:** Rte option case 1 + (--deviate-event-based-com-mapping)
>  ** The issue with this option is similar to case 2: Rte_Rx_000875_status is updated by Rte_COMCbkTOut_{*}, but it is not used by any Rte_Read_{*} function to retrieve the status.
>  ** Another issue is that the Rte_Read_E2E_SWC_* function calls IocRead_Rte_Rx_000875_0(&composite) to get the status, even though the components are on the same core.
>  ** And Rte_ComCbk_*  only update the status via IocWrite_Rte_Rx_000875(&composite), not via local Rte variable.
>  * {*}Case 4{*}:  Rte option case 1 + (-{-}no-optimized-ioc-channels) + ({-}-deviate-event-based-com-mapping)
>  ** The issue with this option is similar to case 3.
>
> Even though I tried the options above, it seems the issue cannot be resolved. Could you check further whether we actually cover this use case in RTA-CAR 12.11.0VCTCESR1pr1?
>
> If not, please confirm whether it can be supported in the official release of RTA-CAR 12.11, or whether there is a bug-fix plan for it.
>
> I have attached the Rte.c files for these 4 cases.
>
> Thanks for your support.
>
